verses.text: “I’ve told you these things so you won’t fall away.
They’ll put you out of the synagogues. The time is coming when anyone who kills you will think they’re serving God.
They’ll do these things because they haven’t known the Father or me.
I’ve told you this so that when the time comes, you’ll remember I warned you. I didn’t tell you from the beginning because I was with you.
But now I’m going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’
Because I’ve told you this, sadness has filled your hearts.
But I’m telling you the truth: It’s better for you that I go away. If I don’t go, the Helper won’t come to you. But if I go, I’ll send him to you.
When he comes, he’ll show the world what sin, righteousness, and judgment mean:
sin, because people don’t believe in me;
righteousness, because I’m going to the Father and you won’t see me anymore;
and judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
“I still have many things to tell you, but you can’t handle them right now.
When the Spirit of truth comes, he’ll guide you into all truth. He won’t speak on his own; he’ll say what he hears and tell you what’s coming.
He’ll glorify me, because he’ll take what belongs to me and make it known to you.
Everything the Father has belongs to me. That’s why I said the Spirit will take what’s mine and make it known to you.
“In a little while, you won’t see me anymore. Then, after a little while, you’ll see me again.”
Some of his disciples said to one another, “What does he mean by, ‘In a little while you won’t see me, and then after a little while you’ll see me again,’ and by, ‘I’m going to the Father’?”
They kept asking, “What does ‘a little while’ mean? We don’t understand what he’s saying.”
Jesus knew they wanted to ask him about this, so he said, “Are you asking each other what I meant when I said, ‘In a little while you won’t see me, and then after a little while you’ll see me again’?
I’m telling you the truth: You’ll cry and grieve, but the world will celebrate. You’ll be sad, but your sadness will turn into joy.
When a woman is giving birth, she has pain because her time has come. But after the baby is born, she no longer remembers the suffering, because she’s happy a child has come into the world.
You’re sad now, but I’ll see you again. Then your hearts will be glad, and no one will take your joy away.
“When that day comes, you won’t ask me anything. I’m telling you the truth: The Father will give you whatever you ask in my name.
Until now, you haven’t asked for anything in my name. Ask, and you’ll receive, so your joy can be complete.
“I’ve been speaking to you in figures of speech. The time is coming when I won’t use figures of speech anymore; I’ll tell you plainly about the Father.
When that day comes, you’ll ask in my name. I’m not saying I’ll ask the Father on your behalf,
because the Father himself loves you. He loves you because you’ve loved me and believed I came from God.
I came from the Father and entered the world. Now I’m leaving the world and going back to the Father.”
His disciples said, “Now you’re speaking clearly, without figures of speech.
Now we know you know everything and don’t need anyone to question you. Because of this, we believe you came from God.”
Jesus answered, “Do you believe now?
The time is coming—in fact, it’s already here—when you’ll all scatter, each to your own place, and leave me alone. But I’m not alone, because the Father is with me.
I’ve told you these things so you can have peace in me. In this world you’ll have trouble. But take heart! I’ve overcome the world.”
